analysis: This batch has documentation-only changes: the new changelog entry changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md (lines 1-8) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md, where the date bump (line 3) and the 'Streaming read' row (line 65) now say that a chunk or field returned whole by one read is kept as read instead of copied into a second buffer (SSDBlockStore.readExactly). The actual Swift change in SSDBlockStore.swift is not supplied, so the documentation is the only evidence. Even so, the described behavior does not touch the T-041 mitigations: AES-256-GCM chunk authentication, the KEK-derived HMAC lookup tags, the identity bindings, the TTL, the disk budget, the descriptor-relative no-follow I/O and the retry raw-byte read budget are all unchanged. The docs still say each chunk is authenticated before use. Dropping one plaintext-adjacent buffer copy (these are ciphertext chunks) does not widen exposure and slightly reduces host memory residency. Two things the next pass should check in the code, neither established by this evidence: (1) readExactly must still enforce the length and bounds checks before allocation, including the maximumChunkBytes caps and the retry raw-byte ceiling charged in SSDCheckpointReadBudget, when it returns the read buffer directly; (2) a partial read must still take the copy/accumulate path, so short reads cannot yield an unauthenticated or truncated chunk. The doc line at ssd-kv-cache.md:278 already cites readExactly in the retry-budget row. No threat-model update is needed from the supplied text. I flag only that the code diff was not available, so these properties are unverified.
